title_orig: The true nature of imposture fully display'd in the life of Mahomet, with a discourse annex'd for the vindicating of Christianity from this charge
title_es: La verdadera naturaleza de la impostura plenamente desplegada en la vida de Mahoma
title_en: The True Nature of Imposture Fully Display'd in the Life of Mahomet
date: c. 1697-1698 (first edition 1697; the copy read is dated 1698 in the archive.org record)
edition_original: London, 1698 (copy read: archive.org thetruenature00priduoft; page images of pp. 54, 158 and 145 read). Pagination as printed.
edition_english: The original is English; quotations are the original text (no separate translation).
licence: Archive.org item; 17th-18th century text, public domain by age. Page images read; the archive.org page does not state a separate licence for the scan.
authenticity_note: Genuine work of Humphrey Prideaux; the age statements are his own, and he writes as an apologist who takes his facts from Arabic and Latin authors (he cites Johannes Andreas, Sionita, Guadagnoli, Thevenot).
notes: Prideaux argues the Prophet's wives were a sign of his lust. The Ayesha passages are at pp. 53-54, 145, 147, 158 of this edition. OCR of pp. 145, 147 and 158 was checked against the page image only for p. 158 and p. 54 (see passages.json).

title_orig: La vie de Mahomet; traduite et compilée de l'Alcoran, des traditions authentiques de la Sonna, et des meilleurs auteurs arabes
title_en: The Life of Mahomet, translated and compiled from the Alcoran, the authentic traditions and Arab authors
genre: Biography compiled from Arabic sources, with a list of the wives
edition_original: Tome premier, second part, 1732; Google Books copy bub_gb_6V-dqz4EQUMC (imprint not checked); pages 328-329 read from page images
digital_url: https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_6V-dqz4EQUMC (page images read: https://archive.org/download/bub_gb_6V-dqz4EQUMC/page/n341&height=1800 = printed p. 329; .../page/n340&height=1000 = printed p. 328)
licence: Public domain by age (1732); scanned by Google/Boston Public Library via archive.org
authenticity_note: Gagnier's own compilation; the age statements derive from the Arabic traditions (Muslim sources), which Gagnier reports.
notes: The OCR text (djvu) mis-reads the numerals on p. 328 (4/5 instead of 40); the quoted passage was copied from the page image.
